tasks.spec:
You are building a text-message appointment-recall pathway for an optometry practice, derived from a signed design map. Your current working directory IS a disposable git worktree. Edit files here directly.

BOUNDARY, read this before anything else.
- You own exactly three files and may create or modify NOTHING else: scripts/build_v22_recall_map.py, scripts/validate_v22.py, tests/test_v22_scenarios.py. You may also write generated output under build/.
- NEVER run git commit, git push, or any git write command. Leave changes uncommitted; the harness exports them.
- NEVER call a network endpoint or external API. Everything you need is on disk. Generation is purely local.
- NEVER load skills, call MCP tools or Apps, or capture notes to any external memory or knowledge base.
- Do not modify anything under contract/ or any existing reference file.

THE CONTRACT IS contract/state-procedure-map.md. Read it in full before writing anything. It is a signed design map, not a suggestion: eight patient states, five actions each with three outcomes, nine possible patient replies, nine numbered rules, and the exact list of 22 node ids. Every node you build must trace to something on that page. If something does not trace back, do not build it.

This is a REBUILD FROM THE MAP, not a patch of the previous version. The previous version is in scripts/build_v21_recall_lanes.py for reference on node and edge SHAPE only. Do not carry its structure across. Specifically, the previous version had three separate nodes representing the single Offered state and a separate clarify node; the map collapses all of that into one n_offer, and rule R2 is what makes that non-negotiable.

REFERENCE MATERIAL ALREADY IN THIS WORKTREE:
- contract/state-procedure-map.md — THE CONTRACT. Read first.
- contract/verified-defects.md, contract/decisions.json, contract/review.json — the history that produced the map. Useful background; the map supersedes them where they differ.
- scripts/build_v20_patient_id.py — reuse its helper shapes: webhook(), waiting(), message(), end(), edge(), sanitize_graph(), normalized(). Do not invent a different node schema.
- scripts/build_v21_recall_lanes.py, scripts/validate_v21.py, tests/test_v21_scenarios.py — the previous revision.
- graph/v20_sanitized.json — the live graph, for node and edge shape.
- docs/mott-eyecloud-endpoint-field-catalog.csv — the gateway contract. Do not invent endpoints, request fields or response paths.
- docs/mott-aws-response-data-inventory.md — approved response mappings per endpoint.

DELIVERABLE 1: scripts/build_v22_recall_map.py
A deterministic generator accepting --out PATH that writes the v22 graph as JSON. Two runs with different output paths must produce byte-identical files.

Build exactly the 22 nodes the map lists, with exactly those ids. The two most important rules are R1 and R9, and together they are the defect that stranded a live conversation.

R9: every comparison value in responsePathways must be a STRING literal. Write "true", "false", "1", never the boolean true or the integer 1. Bland stores values extracted from a webhook response as strings, so a boolean literal never matches, the node falls through to no match at all, and the patient is stranded with no message. The mature production pathway on this same account compares against 'true', '1' and '2' throughout; follow it exactly.

R1: each silent step's conditions must exhaustively cover its routing variable using a != complement, ordered so the UNKNOWN case takes the safe branch and only an explicit expected value takes the consequential one. For a verify step that means exactly this shape:
  ["conflict_ok", "!=", "true",  -> e_safe_failure]
  ["conflict",    "!=", "false", -> n_negotiate]
  ["conflict",    "==", "false", -> n_book_1]
A missing or malformed value then lands on "treat it as not clear" rather than on "book it". Never put the != complement on a booking node. A silent step is not a waiting step, so the 72-hour timeout cannot rescue a fall-through; the complement is the only thing that can.

n_offer is the single Offered state. Its prompt must interpolate patient_first, slot_1_start and slot_2_start, and must NOT interpolate slot_1_end or slot_2_end, because the message shows a start time only per R6. It must name America/New_York as the display timezone, keep the approved Mott Optical copy from the previous version verbatim apart from the time change, handle a reply that mixes a selection with a different preference by clarifying rather than booking, and offer only the first opening when slot_count is one.

n_faq is the only global with enableGlobalAutoReturn true. Its prompt must explicitly forbid inventing, guessing or generating any answer, must carry the single approved fact available today which is the office phone number (855) 750-6688, and must route anything else to the office. Every other global sets enableGlobalAutoReturn false.

e_timeout is NOT global, because silence produces no message for a global to match. Wire it with an explicit labelled edge from each of the three states that actually wait on the patient: n_offer, n_negotiate, n_confirm. n_office and n_faq do not wait, so they get no timeout edge.

Nothing anywhere may claim a suppression, per R8. No node name, tag, outcome or text may assert that a number was suppressed, because no suppression store exists.

No node attaches a tool, per R3. The negotiation lane collects only preference variables in n_negotiate and gets its slot values from the n_search webhook's responseData, which must map slot_count, slot_1_start, slot_1_end, slot_1_doctor, slot_2_start, slot_2_end, slot_2_doctor and time_pref_relaxed.

Unchanged safety invariants: every webhook sets Authorization to exactly {{ SECRET.MottGatewayToken }} and retryAttempts to 0; booking is the /sign route only with verb appt.book and reason new-booking and no allow_conflict; the legacy /book, /reschedule and /cancel routes never appear; n_identity is the only start node and still guards an empty or unresolved recall_patient_id before any gateway call; confirmation is reachable only on a booking success; the mirrored verify and book branches stay; every edge carries a non-empty label; no prompt instructs the model to normalize or compute calendar dates. The graph carries analysis_options whose outcome values include declined and whose fields include faq_answered.

DELIVERABLE 2: scripts/validate_v22.py
A structural validator that loads the generated graph and exits non-zero with a printed reason per violation. It must check every one of the nine rules by number, and each failure message must name the rule it violates. Accept an optional --graph PATH defaulting to build/v22_a.json. Print WHY, not just that something failed.

DELIVERABLE 3: tests/test_v22_scenarios.py
A pytest suite in the style of tests/test_v21_scenarios.py. Cover at minimum: every silent node has a != complement and none of the verify nodes puts that complement on a booking node; every comparison value in every responsePathway is a string literal and never a boolean or an integer; Offered is exactly one node and the banned duplicate nodes do not exist; the offer message contains start times and contains no end times; n_faq auto-returns and every other global does not; e_timeout is not global and is wired from exactly the three waiting states; no node attaches a tool; n_search maps all eight slot fields; no node text or tag claims a suppression; a post-confirmation change request never reaches a booking node; a decline reaches the declined exit and not the opt-out exit. Do not write a test that asserts a property its own helper injects; assert against the generated graph.

HOW TO VERIFY YOUR OWN WORK, from the worktree root:
  mkdir -p build
  python3 scripts/build_v22_recall_map.py --out build/v22_a.json
  python3 scripts/build_v22_recall_map.py --out build/v22_b.json
  diff build/v22_a.json build/v22_b.json
  python3 scripts/validate_v22.py
  python3 -m pytest tests/test_v22_scenarios.py -q

All five must succeed. An independent orchestrator-owned gate also runs against your graph and enforces all eight rules by number, so satisfying only your own validator is not enough. A reference construction satisfying every rule reaches 22 nodes and 36 edges, so this is known buildable; ceilings are 24 nodes and 52 edges.

HARD RULES. Do not invent gateway endpoints, request fields or response paths. Do not weaken a safety invariant to simplify the graph. Do not carry forward the previous version's three-nodes-for-one-state structure. Do not commit. Do not touch any file outside your three owned paths and build/.
tasks.verified: the generator is deterministic and its graph passes an orchestrator-owned gate enforcing all eight map rules by number, including a fallback failure exit on every silent step, one node for the Offered state, start-time-only copy, and the single auto-returning FAQ global
